name: ListItem
summary: One item of a list a person chooses from: a menu's action, a menu's checkbox or radio, or a listbox's option. The one list item every popup list uses, so menus and selects look and behave alike: the same heights, padding, hover, focus, selected and unavailable states, leading slot (icon, avatar, picture, palette or selection mark) and trailing slot (meta, shortcut, submenu chevron or check). Not for navigation (use Navigation) or rows of data (use RowList). Added on the owner's direction (F10, 2026-11-07): "Dropdown list should be custom list using the same list item component." Made exhaustive in F15.8 (Q28, Q42).
a11y: A `div` with the list's role, never focusable by Tab: a menu moves focus onto it, a listbox points at it with `aria-activedescendant` and `active` draws the focus ring, or the hover tint with `activeAppearance="tint"`. Add `activeIndicator` when that mild fill alone lacks 3:1 contrast: its fixed-slot trailing chevron uses the text token; verify that cue against the actual surface. Native focus still draws its ring. Chosen and on are carried by `aria-selected` or `aria-checked` and a mark (check, box or dot), never colour alone. A shortcut sets `aria-keyshortcuts`; a submenu sets `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Size s is a written target exception (32 px, above the 24 px minimum) that returns to 44 px on a coarse pointer. The fills reach the item's edges and never touch a neighbour's: the list owns a gap between items. A `row` (a grid list) has its words, meta and trailing controls as `gridcell`s; the list moves focus. A `button` (an on-page action list) is its own Tab stop and runs on Enter or Space; `drillIn` adds the chevron. A `listitem` is static: no Tab stop, no hover; a control in its `trailing` slot is its own Tab stop. `inactive` stays reachable so its reason is read; `busy` sets `aria-busy`; unread adds ", unread" to the name for assistive technology. With `href` it is an `a[href]` with the same role, look, focus and keyboard: the browser's link menu and middle-click work, and Enter follows it.

props.name: role
props.description: The item's role in its list: `option` in a Select's listbox; `menuitem` for an action in a MenuButton's menu; `menuitemcheckbox` for an on/off setting kept in a menu; `menuitemradio` for one choice of a group in a menu; `listitem` for an item of a static list, which isn't itself chosen and may hold a control in `trailing`; `button` for an action in an action list on the page (its own Tab stop; Enter or Space runs it); `row` for a row of a grid list, whose words, meta and trailing controls are its cells.

props.name: label
props.description: The item's name, in sentence case.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting words under the name: what choosing it does or gives. Wraps to at most two lines.

props.name: descriptionPosition
props.description: `block` (default) puts the description under the name; `inline` beside it, for a short qualifier ("main", "@asha").

props.name: size
props.description: `s` 32 px for dense desktop menus (44 px on a coarse pointer), `normal` 44 px, `l` 56 px for avatars and pictures. Default `normal`.

props.name: layout
props.description: `row` (default) lays the item out in a line. `tile` stacks the icon above the name and the description in a control's surface, for a catalogue of things to add (ActionList `layout="tiles"` sets it). An action only.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon from the active set.

props.name: inset
props.description: Keep the icon column empty so this item's words line up with siblings that have icons.

props.name: avatar
props.description: A person or team: a round picture, or the initials of `name` when there's no picture. Decorative: the label names it.

props.name: thumbnail
props.description: A lazy square picture of the item. On failure its fixed slot shows `icon`, or the image icon. Decorative: the label names it.

props.name: preview
props.description: Up to four #rrggbb colours shown as a strip before the name, for items that are palettes. Decorative.

props.name: meta
props.description: Short trailing words or a number: a count, a state, a time. Never a second name.

props.name: truncate
props.description: One line, whatever the width: the name and the meta each end in an ellipsis when there isn't room, the meta giving way first (it shrinks ten times faster) and sitting at the end. For dense result lists where every row must keep one height. The full words stay in the item for assistive technology. Off by default: words wrap.

props.name: nameLines
props.description: Clamps the name to this many lines (LR153), ending in an ellipsis; the full words stay for assistive technology. For an entry whose name is a person's own words (a comment, a note). Left out: the name wraps in full. Not with `truncate`.

props.name: current
props.description: The item that is open beside the list now (LR153): `aria-current="true"` and the selected fill, so a list of entries shows which one its detail, popover or canvas has open. For an action or a static item; an option uses `selected`.

props.name: shortcut
props.description: The keys that do the same thing, as the platform writes them (e.g. "Ctrl+C"). Sets `aria-keyshortcuts`.

props.name: submenu
props.description: Opens a submenu: shows the chevron and sets `aria-haspopup`. A `menuitem` only.

props.name: drillIn
props.description: Opens a deeper level in place (a settings page, a folder): shows the trailing chevron. A `button` only; the label names where it goes.

props.name: tone
props.description: `danger` for an action that destroys or can't be undone (Delete, Remove). The word says it; colour adds to it.

props.name: selected
props.description: For an option: it's chosen (`aria-selected`). For a menu checkbox or radio: it's on (`aria-checked`).

props.name: multiple
props.description: For an option in a listbox that allows several: shows a check box at the start instead of the trailing check.

props.name: mark
props.description: For a single-choice option: how its chosen state shows. `check` (default) the trailing check over the fill; `fill` the fill alone, for a list whose chosen row is where you are (a form's sections), where what shows beside it already says so.

props.name: active
props.description: The keyboard is on it while focus stays on the control (`aria-activedescendant`); shows the focus ring.

props.name: activeAppearance
props.description: Proxy focus from aria-activedescendant: the existing ring, or the same mild fill as hover. Native focus keeps its ring.

props.name: activeIndicator
props.description: Reserve a trailing chevron that shows only on the active item: a non-border cue when a mild tint alone lacks 3:1 contrast.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shown but can't be chosen now (`aria-disabled`); the keyboard skips it. Use when the reason is obvious.

props.name: inactive
props.description: Looks unavailable, but the keyboard still reaches it so its reason (the description) is read: an outage, a missing permission.

props.name: busy
props.description: Its action is running: the compact Progress replaces the leading visual and `aria-busy` is set; the label stays.

props.name: unread
props.description: Not read yet: a heavier name and a dot, with "Unread" for assistive technology.

props.name: expanded
props.description: For an item that shows or hides child items: the chevron turns and `aria-expanded` is set. The list renders the children.

props.name: trailing
props.description: A trailing element: a Badge; for a `listitem` also an icon-only Button (remove, more). Never a control inside an option or menu item.

props.name: id
props.description: Needed for `aria-activedescendant`.

props.name: href
props.description: Goes somewhere: the item renders as a real link (`a[href]`) that keeps its role, so middle-click, Ctrl or Cmd-click, "Open link in new tab" and "Copy link address" work on a menu item, an option or an action. Inside the core `Router` it goes through `router.href()`, as Button with `href` does. Unavailable or busy, the href is left off. With it, `onClick` and `itemRef` receive the anchor; call `event.preventDefault()` to take a plain click over.

props.name: tabbable
props.description: For a `row`: the one row the Tab key reaches (the grid list moves it with the arrows).

props.name: itemRef
props.description: Receives the element, for a list that moves focus between its items.
